ecological_question: As Adélie island populations decline, do breeders become increasingly concentrated among the remaining colony-code breeding components faster than expected from abundance decline and independent counting error alone?

motivation.source: Reviewer-style ecological audit after the hierarchy count-error result
motivation.external_context: Independent Torgersen mapping documents contraction from 23 historic active subcolonies to five active footprints by 2022 and habitat-structured extinction.

eligible_units.gate: unchanged colony-code roster across the complete synchronized census
eligible_units.note: Litchfield contributes only positive-total years to its concentration slope.

metric.name: effective_colony_number
metric.formula: N_eff = (sum_j n_j)^2 / sum_j n_j^2 = 1 / sum_j p_j^2
metric.observed_statistic: OLS slope of annual N_eff against centered calendar year within each island, using years with positive observed island total.
metric.direction: more negative slope = progressive concentration of breeders into fewer/effectively dominant colony-code components

fixed_null.latent_composition: time-invariant pooled colony-code shares estimated from cumulative 1991-2017 breeding-pair counts within each island
fixed_null.annual_total: observed island total retained as the latent annual total
fixed_null.interpretation: No biological redistribution among colony-code components; all apparent N_eff change arises from the declining total and observation error.
fixed_null.implementation_reuse: Same pooled latent state and Poisson / Gamma-Poisson error family as PALMER_HIERARCHY_COUNT_ERROR_NULL_V1.

primary_inference.island_tail: one-sided probability that a fixed-composition/error-only draw has an N_eff slope <= the observed island slope
primary_inference.joint_tail: one-sided probability that all three simulated island slopes are simultaneously <= their observed island-specific slopes
primary_inference.support_rule: Each island-specific p <= 0.05 and the three-island joint p <= 0.05 under all three frozen error models.

interpretation_boundary: A supported result indicates progressive concentration/reorganization beyond simple abundance decline and the frozen independent count-error family.
It does not identify which physical nesting polygons were lost because colony codes are not crosswalked one-to-one to GIS subcolonies.
It does not identify snow, topography, predation, dispersal or habitat quality as the causal mechanism.
The external Torgersen spatial reconstruction is independent phenomenon-level triangulation, not identifier-level validation.
No alternate concentration index, time window, intermediate CV value, or colony-roster reconciliation may be introduced to rescue the endpoint.
